newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle at standstill- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle at standstill- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were at a standstill, with no sales expected until midweek, feedlot sources said.
Packers reportedly had adequate live inventories lined up following last week's heavy trading, they said.
There were scattered bids early at $65.00 per cwt that were passed by owners who were asking $67.00 to $68.00, the feedlot sources said. Sales last week were brisk at $66.00.
Feedlot cattle prices this week were expected to be supported by light supplies of finished cattle, they said.
Cattle weights have been running well below year-ago levels because of the pulling forward of marketings to meet strong packer demand.
Support also was expected from last week's extremely cold weather across the Plains, which impeded cattle development, they said.
Cattle this week were seen improving amid warmer temperatures and dry yards in Kansas and the Texas/western Oklahoma Panhandle, the sources said.
Showlists this week were expected steady to slightly larger than last week, the feedlot sources said.
